blocks.content: This lesson demonstrates every block type supported by Lesson Workbench. Use it to visually inspect and interact with each renderer. Try selecting text and pressing Annotate — then click the yellow marker to edit your note.

Explanation blocks render body text with a gold difficulty widget and a comment textarea below the block. You can select any portion of this text and annotate it — the selected text becomes highlighted with a golden underline. Click the highlighted text to edit the annotation note.

blocks.statement: A rule states a principle followed by concrete examples.
examples: Example 1: The JVM's thread dump shows all Java threads and their stack traces.
Example 2: A thread in BLOCKED state is waiting to acquire a monitor lock owned by another thread.
Example 3: Use Ctrl+\ (or SIGQUIT) to trigger a thread dump on Linux without killing the process.

blocks.prompt: What is the purpose of the `synchronized` keyword in Java?
Which tool can you use to capture a thread dump on Linux without killing the process?

items: Read the thread dump and identify blocked threads
Check which monitor lock each blocked thread is waiting on
Look for the thread that currently owns the contested lock
Verify the owning thread's stack trace for the root cause
Document findings and propose a fix

blocks.claim: A thread dump captures only the current stack trace of a single thread.
blocks.correction: A thread dump captures the stack traces of ALL live threads in the JVM, including their states (RUNNABLE, BLOCKED, WAITING, TIMED_WAITING) and lock information.
